task.text: Humanity disappeared, and the world is restored to a Pleistocene situation, a time period in which humans still didn’t cause any notable extinction at all. Would there be some extinct species of your choice that you would add, that are from time periods before the Pleistocene and that didn't exist in the Pleistocene? If yes what species and why?

attempts.high: Imagine humanity is gone and Earth resets to a Pleistocene baseline, back before humans drove anything extinct. Here's the fun part — you get to play god of de-extinction. Pick any species from time periods BEFORE the Pleistocene that you'd reintroduce into this restored world. Totally your call which ones, however many you like, from whatever era. Build out your reasoning, paint the picture of how they'd fit. Surprise me with the choices.
attempts.low: Imagine humanity is gone and Earth resets to a Pleistocene baseline, back before humans drove anything extinct. Consider exactly these three pre-Pleistocene species for reintroduction: Tyrannosaurus rex, Dunkleosteus, and Arthropleura. For each one, state in 2–3 sentences whether it could plausibly survive in a Pleistocene-restored world and why or why not, based on climate and ecosystem fit. Cover only these three, in this order, no additional species.
